## Verdict

Inkwell costs least for a team of 9, at $80 per month. Its 10-seat minimum means the team pays for one seat it will not use, but at $8 per seat that penalty is small enough to keep it ahead of Dorado's $171 and Borealis's $300.

## Vendor pricing

| Vendor | Price per seat | Minimum seats |
|---|---|---|
| Dorado | $19 | 1 |
| Inkwell | $8 | 10 |
| Borealis | $12 | 25 |

## Cost at this size

Seats paid for is the team size (9) or the vendor minimum, whichever is larger.

- **Dorado:** minimum 1 is below 9, so 9 seats paid. 9 × $19 = **$171 per month**.
- **Inkwell:** minimum 10 exceeds 9, so 10 seats paid. 10 × $8 = **$80 per month**. One unused seat, worth $8.
- **Borealis:** minimum 25 exceeds 9, so 25 seats paid. 25 × $12 = **$300 per month**. Sixteen unused seats, worth $192.

Inkwell is $91 per month cheaper than Dorado and $220 cheaper than Borealis — $1,092 and $2,640 over twelve months. Effective rate per working person: Inkwell $8.89, Dorado $19.00, Borealis $33.33.

## Risks

The ranking is stable as the team grows. Inkwell has the lowest per-seat rate on the list, so it stays cheapest at every size above 9; its unused seat disappears at 10 people. Shrinking matters more: below 5 people Dorado overtakes Inkwell, since Inkwell's $80 floor holds while Dorado bills only for seats used.

Borealis never becomes price-competitive here. Its $300 is fixed until 25 people, at which point Inkwell costs $200 — still $100 less.

This compares list price only. The price list carries no information on features, support tiers, usage limits or security posture, so a cheaper seat may not be the same product. All figures assume monthly billing as stated; annual commitments, volume discounts and onboarding fees are not on the list and could change the result.
